sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time: 2026-11-13 02:36 UTC. Scope: weekly. Date range: 2026-11-06 through 2026-11-13 (GitHub Trending “This week”, rolling seven-day view). Ranking: listed Trending weekly star gains sorted descending.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: This week’s signal is the move from agent prompts to agent work surfaces: reusable skill packs and tools that let agents operate browsers, desktops, security workflows and enterprise data. Cloudflare’s audit skill and OpenMausBot lead on weekly star velocity.

sections.title: Top Repositories
sections.content: The 11 repositories below are ordered by weekly stars gained, descending; each entry includes its primary language, total stars, and why it matters.

sections.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
sections.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
sections.why_notable: +10,700 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents security in this snapshot.
sections.architecture_summary: A security-audit workflow that divides reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation and independent verification into auditable steps.
sections.workflow: Uses a coverage ledger, isolated hunters and fresh verifiers; emits schema-validated findings and target-neutral reports.

sections.title: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
sections.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use
sections.why_notable: +9,104 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents agent apps in this snapshot.
sections.unique_caveat: Independent project; its README says it is not affiliated with xAI, Meta, OpenAI or Manus.
sections.architecture_summary: A local-first team of chat-based AI agents, each with its own personality, model, connected apps and cloud computer; users can watch and approve work.
sections.workflow: A desktop/chat product wraps agent runtimes such as Claude or Codex and provisions a computer for each bot.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
sections.why_notable: +8,731 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents agent skills in this snapshot.
sections.architecture_summary: An opinionated set of small, adaptable, model-agnostic engineering skills, designed to be composable rather than impose a single development process.
sections.workflow: Install through agent-specific plugin/marketplace routes or copy editable skill files; user chooses one update model per agent.

sections.title: vercel-labs/agent-desktop
sections.description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
sections.why_notable: +6,414 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents agent interfaces in this snapshot.
sections.unique_caveat: Snapshots, clipboard reads and other outputs can contain private desktop content; avoid public logs/uploads.
sections.architecture_summary: Cross-platform computer-use CLI reads desktop accessibility trees as JSON and lets an agent act on referenced controls without pixel matching.
sections.workflow: Agent snapshots the UI, acts on a reference, then snapshots again to verify; the tool contains no model and also ships a C library.

sections.title: anthropics/skills
sections.why_notable: +6,055 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents agent skills in this snapshot.
sections.architecture_summary: Folders of task-specific instructions, scripts and resources dynamically loaded to give Claude repeatable workflows, with worked examples across technical, creative, enterprise and document tasks.
sections.workflow: Each skill lives in a self-contained folder; the repository is an implementation/examples collection for Claude rather than the universal Agent Skills specification.

sections.title: NVIDIA/auto-ontology
sections.description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.
sections.why_notable: +5,802 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents grounded analytics in this snapshot.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says the project is currently not accepting external contributions.
sections.architecture_summary: Builds an enterprise semantic/ontology layer from metadata, connecting business meaning, entities, relationships, lineage and provenance for agentic analytics.
sections.workflow: Provides a catalog and ontology over relational sources, natural-language-to-SQL, query validation against certified definitions, and MCP/CLI/API access.

sections.title: D4Vinci/Scrapling
sections.description: 🕷️ The BEST Web Scraping framework that handles everything from a single request to a full-scale crawl!
sections.why_notable: +4,743 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents developer tools in this snapshot.
sections.architecture_summary: Python scraping toolkit aimed at scaling from one-off requests to crawls across modern sites.
sections.workflow: README presents a framework spanning request handling and crawler workflows; detailed component design is not summarized here.

sections.title: vercel-labs/agent-browser
sections.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
sections.why_notable: +4,601 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents agent interfaces in this snapshot.
sections.architecture_summary: Native Rust CLI gives agents a persistent browser controlled through compact accessibility snapshots and element refs, followed by explicit re-observation after actions.
sections.workflow: Shell-driven loop: open, snapshot, act on a ref, inspect the result; stale refs require a fresh snapshot.

sections.title: zed-industries/zed
sections.description: Code at the speed of thought – Zed is a high-performance, multiplayer code editor from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter.
sections.why_notable: +2,339 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents developer tools in this snapshot.
sections.architecture_summary: High-performance collaborative code editor built in Rust, an established editor project rather than a new agent-only package.
sections.workflow: N/A - not available from GitHub README review in this snapshot.

sections.description: Agent Skills for Google products and technologies
sections.why_notable: +1,933 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents agent skills in this snapshot.
sections.architecture_summary: Google-maintained skill examples for its products and technologies, extending the cross-vendor agent-skill packaging pattern.
sections.workflow: N/A - not available from GitHub README review in this snapshot.

sections.description: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.
sections.why_notable: +1,671 stars on GitHub Trending weekly; represents simulation in this snapshot.
sections.architecture_summary: Physics simulator for multi-joint dynamics and contact, a notable non-agent outlier in a week dominated by agent-facing tools.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content:
- **Packaged agent skills:** Reusable skill directories are a major signal: anthropics/skills, mattpocock/skills and google/skills publish task-specific guidance/resources rather than another general-purpose model.
- **Agents gain browser and desktop controls:** vercel-labs/agent-browser and vercel-labs/agent-desktop share a shell-driven observe-act-observe model using accessibility references instead of opaque pixel-only actions.
- **Grounding agents in enterprise data:** NVIDIA/auto-ontology emphasizes semantic context, lineage and deterministic query validation to make agentic analytics more explainable.
- **Security workflows for coding agents:** cloudflare/security-audit-skill treats audit output as a verified pipeline with coverage tracking and machine-readable findings.
- **Personalized agent applications:** milind-soni/OpenMausBot packages multiple agents into a local-first chat product, each with an individual model, apps and computer.
- **Established developer tools remain in the mix:** D4Vinci/Scrapling, zed-industries/zed and agent-browser show interest in scraping, coding and browser automation infrastructure, not just agent prompts.
- **A non-agent outlier:** google-deepmind/mujoco is the lone physics-simulation entry among the 11 listed repositories, a useful counterpoint to the agent-heavy cluster.
- **Languages:** Python 4, Rust 3, TypeScript 1, JavaScript 1, Shell 1 and C++ 1 across the 11 listed repos.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The most visible shift inside this snapshot is toward packaged, auditable agent capability: skills, controlled computer-use interfaces and verification-oriented workflows, rather than just another agent framework. The strongest practical differentiators are observable actions and grounding—accessibility-tree interactions, independent security checks, and data provenance. MuJoCo and Zed remind us that general-purpose developer and simulation tools still attract substantial interest.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary: https://github.com/trending?since=weekly, captured 2026-11-13 02:36 UTC. Corroboration: GitHub REST repository and default-branch commit lookups where available (first eight repositories); remaining three current default-branch SHAs were checked from GitHub repository-page currentOid metadata. Trending-page stars and languages were cross-checked against those page/API values. GitHub REST began rate-limiting after several repository lookups. Current READMEs consulted for the narration-priority projects: cloudflare/security-audit-skill, milind-soni/OpenMausBot, mattpocock/skills, vercel-labs/agent-desktop, anthropics/skills, NVIDIA/auto-ontology, D4Vinci/Scrapling and vercel-labs/agent-browser. Weekly star gains come from the matching GitHub Trending view; this report sorts those displayed gains descending. No prior-week comparison is claimed.
